output.findings:

Top Rust Repos: 
1. farion1231/cc-switch (7,357 stars this week): A cross-platform desktop All-in-One assistant for various coding agents like Claude Code and Gemini CLI. 
2. ruvnet/RuView (4,298 stars this week): Provides spatial intelligence and presence detection, useful for advanced agentic environment awareness.

4. openai/codex (2,173 stars this week): A lightweight coding agent designed for terminal-based workflows. 
5. iii-hq/iii (1,461 stars this week): A service composition and observation tool for real-time agentic systems. 
6. ogulcancelik/herdr (1,206 stars this week): An agent multiplexer for terminal-based agent orchestration. 

Top Python Repos: 
1. microsoft/markitdown (11,962 stars this week): A critical utility for converting diverse office documents into Markdown, streamlining data preparation for LLM agents. 
2. anthropics/skills (4,633 stars this week): A public repository of agent skills, essential for standardizing agent capabilities. 
3. mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (4,330 stars this week): Provides structured cybersecurity skills for agents, mapped to major industry frameworks. 
4. anthropics/claude-code (3,004 stars this week): An agentic coding tool that integrates directly into the terminal for codebase management and git workflows. 
5. chopratejas/headroom (1,868 stars this week): A token-optimization tool that compresses logs and RAG chunks, offering a library, proxy, and MCP server implementation. 
6. microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit (1,529 stars this week): Provides essential policy enforcement and security sandboxing for autonomous agents.

prompt_sent:
You are the GitHub Research skill. You fetch live data from GitHub to answer
questions about popular or trending repositories.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the specific sub-question/task from the INPUTS list (look at the first literal value). If no specific task is in the INPUTS, read the overall USER_QUERY. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`, default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, total stars, stars gained (or weekly/monthly stars depending on the window), and URL. In your `findings`, list each repo clearly with its description, total stars, and stars gained so that downstream nodes can extract these fields.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

Output schema (JSON, no prose, no markdown fences):

  {
    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
    "sources": [{"url": "<url>", "title": "<title>"}, ...],
    "findings": "<2–6 short paragraphs of normalised text>"
  }

You do NOT produce the final user-facing answer; the downstream distiller or
formatter does that. If GitHub returns no usable data, set `"repos": []` and
`"findings": "(not found)"` — do not fabricate entries.
